title: Which warm-up included the most minutes of easy movement?
explanation: The dance warm-up lasted six minutes. Easy movement is one way to get warmed up.

title: What does a physical therapist mainly help people do?
options: Move and do everyday activities more easily
explanation: Physical therapists help people improve how they move and take part in activities that matter to them.

title: I bend and straighten so you can sit down and stand up. I join your thigh to your lower leg. What am I?
explanation: Your knee bends when you sit and straightens when you stand.
hint: I sit right above your shin.

title: Which activity is a good example of practicing balance?
options: Standing on one foot near a support
explanation: Standing on one foot gives you a narrower base and challenges your balance.

title: True or false? Physical therapy can help people who don’t play sports.
explanation: Physical therapists work with people of all ages on things like walking, balance, recovery and daily tasks.

title: Which part of your body bends when you bring a spoon toward your mouth?
explanation: Your elbow bends to bring your hand closer to your face.

title: Tap through the movement. In which frame is the knee bent the most?
explanation: The knee is most bent in the last frame. The angle between the thigh and lower leg is smallest there.

title: Rana wants to get better at climbing the stairs at home. Which goal fits her best?
options: Walk up her stairs more easily
explanation: In physical therapy, goals often come from everyday tasks the person wants to do.

title: You rise onto your tiptoes to reach a high shelf. Which muscles are helping lift your heels?
explanation: Your calf muscles help point the foot and raise the heel.
hint: They’re on the back of your lower leg.

title: True or false? A physical therapist might give you exercises to practice at home.
explanation: Home practice can help you build on what you learn during your sessions.

title: What would be useful to tell your physical therapist at a first visit?
options: Which movements are hard for you
What color shoes they should wear
The name of your favorite singer
explanation: Knowing what is hard and what you want to do helps the therapist plan with you.

title: Which player stood on one foot for the longest time?
explanation: Karim held the position for 12 seconds. Timing a task is one way to track progress.

title: Which movement would a therapist watch to learn how you get up from a chair?
explanation: Watching the actual task helps the therapist see which part feels difficult.

title: Which body part connects your foot to your lower leg?
explanation: Your ankle lets your foot move relative to your lower leg.

title: I help your foot clear the ground when you walk. What movement am I?
options: Lifting your toes toward your shin
explanation: Lifting your toes toward your shin is called ankle dorsiflexion. It helps clear the foot during a step.
hint: Imagine lifting the front of your foot while your heel stays on the floor.

title: Which move best practices reaching for an object on a shelf?
options: Rolling a ball under a table
Reaching up to place a light object on a shelf
explanation: Practicing a version of the real task can help you build the skill you need.

title: Which day showed the longest walk?
explanation: Day 2 reached eight minutes. A walking log can help someone and their therapist see patterns.

title: True or false? Two people with sore shoulders might get different exercise plans.
explanation: Plans can differ because people have different goals, movements and symptoms.

title: Which tool might a physical therapist use to count how long you can balance?
explanation: A stopwatch measures time, so you can compare repeated attempts under the same conditions.
hint: It also comes in handy when timing a race.

title: You’ve been practicing getting up from a chair. Which change best shows that the task is getting easier?
options: You can stand with less help from your hands
Your chair is a different color
explanation: Using less hand support is one practical sign that standing up has become easier for you.

title: Which move used the fewest repetitions in this practice log?
explanation: Sit-to-stands had four repetitions. A repetition is one time through a move.

title: True or false? Walking, climbing stairs and getting up from a chair can all be physical therapy goals.
explanation: Each task uses movement skills that can matter in daily life.

title: You want to see if your balance improved. Which makes a fair comparison?
options: Use a different surface every time
Time one foot today and the other foot next week
Use the same foot, surface and setup each time
explanation: Keeping the setup the same lets you compare attempts more fairly.

title: I can stretch, pull back and make an exercise feel harder. You might see me in a clinic. What am I?
explanation: A resistance band adds a pulling force that you can work against as you move.
hint: I look a bit like a big elastic band.

title: Maya wants to return to her dance group. Which plan best matches her goal?
options: Practice dance-related moves in manageable steps
Change to a goal chosen by someone else
explanation: Therapy can include gradual practice of movements that matter to the person.

title: Which session included the longest rest between activities?
explanation: Session A had a four-minute rest. The amount of rest changes how a session feels.

title: What’s a good way to tell your therapist how an exercise went?
options: Say which part felt easy or difficult
Guess the answer they want to hear
Only tell them how many people were in the room
explanation: Specific feedback helps both of you decide what to practice or adjust next.

title: What is one repetition of sitting down and standing back up?
options: Sitting down and standing up once
explanation: One repetition is one full time through the exercise.

title: A friend says “بدي ارجع امشي مع رفقاتي” — “I want to walk with my friends again.” Which goal matches what they care about?
options: Walk the short route their friends use
explanation: A goal is more useful when it matches the activity the person wants to return to.
hint: Focus on the activity they want to do with their friends.

title: After a knee injury, Alex wants to walk to the park again. What could a physical therapist do first?
options: Ask about the goal and see how Alex walks now
Ignore the walk and only count push-ups
Promise a full recovery by tomorrow
explanation: Physical therapy starts by understanding what matters to the person and checking how they move today.
